newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Scor debuts on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: France's Scor debuts on Wall Street.

text.p: Leading French reinsurer Scor made a strong debut on Wall Street on Thursday and announced that European and U.S. institutional investors had snapped up 30 percent of its capital sold by insurer UAP.

Scor, the world's sixth largest reinsurer by turnover, said UAP's initial offering of seven million shares or 26 percent of Scor's capital was more than four times oversubscribed, leading UAP to boost the placement to eight million shares.
"It was a very successful operation which will give us a very big visibility," said Scor managing director Serge Osouf.
Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP), which had held around 41 percent of the reinsurer, said it sold the Scor shares at 197 francs ($38.02) per share.
UAP timed the share offering to coincide with Scor's listing on Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange.

Scor announced in June it would seek a New York listing "as Wall Street was the main trading for reinsurance shares in the world." It said the move was part of a drive to broaden its shareholder base as it expands its global reach.

Scor shares finished up 1.99 percent at 205 francs with traders saying investors unable to purchase shares from UAP were now buying them in the market. UAP shares ended down 0.64 percent at 108.20 francs.
The Scor shares climbed on Wall Street, rising 1-1/4 to $39-3/8 in early trade.

"This success marks the final stage in the modification of Scor's share ownership," Scor said. It said it now had "an international share ownership made up mainly of European institutional investors and investment funds as well as U.S. investors."
Scor said some 3.3 million shares were placed in the United States and 5.9 million shares were placed in Europe. A small number were placed in Asia.
A UAP spokesman said the sale of the Scor shares would generate up to 1.8 billion francs of which 1.4 billion would be used to cut debt. It would make no capital gain on the sale, it said.
In addition to expanding the number of shares on offer, UAP gave underwriters a "greenshoe" option to buy up to another 1.2 million Scor shares to cover over-allotments.
The UAP spokesman said the group expected its final holding in Scor to be around 12 percent, after transactions involving convertible bonds, and plans to hold that stake.
UAP acquired its Scor stake partly through its sale to Scor of its own reinsurance unit in 1989.

Scor said it had assembled a group of long-term investors, including UAP, to hold 20 percent of the capital and added that membership of its board of directors would be changed soon to reflect the new make-up of the share ownership. ($1=5.181 French Franc)
